text: The FBI is issuing this announcement to ask the public to report information about PRC-affiliated activity publicly tracked as "Salt Typhoon" and the compromise of multiple US telecommunications companies.
location: FBI announcement, opening paragraph

text: This activity resulted in the theft of call data logs, a limited number of private communications involving identified victims, and the copying of select information subject to court-ordered US law enforcement requests.
location: FBI announcement, opening paragraph

text: Additionally, OFAC is sanctioning Sichuan Juxinhe Network Technology Co., LTD., a Sichuan-based cybersecurity company with direct involvement in the Salt Typhoon cyber group.
location: Treasury press release, opening paragraph

text: This activity partially overlaps with cyber threat actor reporting by the cybersecurity industry—commonly referred to as Salt Typhoon, OPERATOR PANDA, RedMike, UNC5807, and GhostEmperor, among others. The authoring agencies are not adopting a particular commercial naming convention.
location: Joint advisory, opening section, page 1

text: The YARA rule SALT_TYPHOON_CMD1_SFTP_CLIENT contains the strings "monitor capture CAP", "export ftp://%s:%s@%s%s", "main.CapExport", "main.SftpDownload", and ".(*SSHClient).CommandShell".
location: Joint advisory, page 21, Cmd1 SFTP client YARA rule

text: The YARA rule SALT_TYPHOON_NEW2_SFTP_CLIENT contains the strings "invoke_shell", "execute_commands", "cmd_file", "stop_event", "decrypt_message", "COMMANDS_FILE", "RUN_TIME", "LOG_FILE", "ENCRYPTION_PASSWORD", and "FIREWALL_ADDRESS".
location: Joint advisory, page 21, New2 SFTP client YARA rule

text: People’s Republic of China (PRC) state-sponsored cyber threat actors are targeting networks globally, including, but not limited to, telecommunications, government, transportation, lodging, and military infrastructure networks.
location: Joint advisory, Executive Summary, page 1

text: Three network devices registered to a Canadian telecommunications company were compromised by likely Salt Typhoon actors in mid-February 2025.
location: PDF page 2, The threat to Canadian organizations

text: The actors exploited CVE-2023-20198 to retrieve the running configuration files from all three devices and modified at least one of the files to configure a GRE tunnel, enabling traffic collection from the network.
location: PDF page 2, The threat to Canadian organizations

text: The responsible actors are almost certainly PRC state-sponsored actors, specifically Salt Typhoon.
location: PDF page 2, The threat to Canadian organizations

text: While not an exhaustive list, the table below highlights some of the CVEs known to have been exploited by Salt Typhoon.
location: Tenable article, section: Known CVEs commonly exploited by Salt Typhoon, paragraph before CVE table

text: Of these five CVEs, four of them were exploited in the wild as zero-day vulnerabilities. While it’s unknown if Salt Typhoon exploited any of these flaws as zero-days, the level of sophistication from the group does suggest it has the technical ability to develop and exploit zero-day flaws in its attacks.
location: Tenable article, section: Known CVEs commonly exploited by Salt Typhoon, paragraph after CVE table

text: Investigations associated with these APT actors indicate that they are having considerable success exploiting publicly known common vulnerabilities and exposures (CVEs) and other avoidable weaknesses within compromised infrastructure [T1190]. Exploitation of zero-day vulnerabilities has not been observed to date.
location: Joint advisory, Initial access, page 6

text: The APT actors leverage infrastructure, such as virtual private servers (VPSs) [T1583.003] and compromised intermediate routers [T1584.008], that have not been attributable to a publicly known botnet or obfuscation network infrastructure to target telecommunications and network service providers, including ISPs [T1090].
location: Joint advisory, Initial access, page 7

text: To maintain persistent access to target networks, the APT actors use a variety of techniques. Notably, a number of these techniques can obfuscate the actors’ source IP address in system logs, as their actions may be recorded as originating from local IP addresses [T1027].
location: Joint advisory, Persistence, page 8

text: Following initial access, the APT actors target protocols and infrastructure involved in authentication—such as Terminal Access Controller Access Control System Plus (TACACS+)—to facilitate lateral movement across network devices, often through SNMP enumeration and SSH. From these devices, the APT actors passively collect packet capture (PCAP) from specific ISP customer networks [T1040] [T1005].
location: Joint advisory, Lateral movement & collection, page 10

text: Provider-held data, such as: Subscriber information; User content; Customer records and metadata; Network diagrams, inventories, device configurations, and vendor lists; Passwords.
location: Joint advisory, Lateral movement & collection, page 10

text: Analysis indicates that the APT actors leverage separate (potentially multiple) command and control channels for exfiltration to conceal their data theft within the noise of high-traffic nodes, such as proxies and Network Address Translation (NAT) pools. The APT actors often use tunnels, such as IPsec and GRE, to conduct C2 and exfiltration activities [T1048.003].
location: Joint advisory, Exfiltration, page 13

text: The APT actors collected PCAPs using native tooling on the compromised system, with the primary objective likely being to capture TACACS+ traffic over TCP port 49.
location: Joint advisory, Case study: Collecting native PCAP, page 13

text: As part of this campaign, PRC cyber actors are targeting these network devices, exploiting existing vulnerabilities to gain and maintain access to TSPs.
location: Canada/FBI bulletin, PRC cyber actors exploit vulnerabilities in edge devices, page 3

text: Salt Typhoon has been active since at least 2019 and has been responsible for numerous compromises of U.S. companies in the communication sector.
location: Treasury press release, section: Chinese malicious cyber group SALT TYPHOON

text: Sichuan Juxinhe Network Technology Co., LTD. (Sichuan Juxinhe) had direct involvement in the exploitation of these U.S. telecommunication and internet service provider companies.
location: Treasury press release, section: Sichuan Juxinhe Network Technology Co., LTD.

text: Investigations associated with these APT actors indicate that they are having considerable success exploiting publicly known common vulnerabilities and exposures (CVEs) and other avoidable weaknesses within compromised infrastructure. Exploitation of zero-day vulnerabilities has not been observed to date. Example exploited CVEs include CVE-2024-21887, CVE-2024-3400, CVE-2023-20273, CVE-2023-20198, and CVE-2018-0171.
location: Joint advisory, Initial access, page 6

text: While exploiting CVE-2023-20198, the APT actors used the Web Services Management Agent (WSMA) endpoints /webui_wsma_Http or /webui_wsma_Https to bypass authentication and create unauthorized administrative accounts.
location: Joint advisory, Initial access, page 6

text: To maintain persistent access, the APT actors modify Access Control Lists (ACLs) to permit traffic from actor-controlled IP addresses, open standard and non-standard ports, enable SSH servers on network devices, add keys to existing SSH services, and enable or abuse built-in HTTP/HTTPS management servers.
location: Joint advisory, Persistence, page 8

text: To further support discovery and lateral movement, the APT actors may target authentication protocols including TACACS+ and RADIUS, Managed Information Base (MIB), router interfaces, and Resource Reservation Protocol (RSVP) sessions.
location: Joint advisory, Lateral movement & collection, page 10

text: The APT actors collect network information including BGP routes, installed software and configuration files. They also capture in-transit network traffic using SPAN, RSPAN or ERSPAN capabilities available on routers.
location: Joint advisory, Lateral movement & collection, page 10–11

text: The APT actors capture RADIUS or TACACS+ authentication traffic using router packet-capture capabilities. They may also redirect TACACS+ server configurations to actor-controlled IP addresses to capture authentication attempts.
location: Joint advisory, Lateral movement & collection, page 11

text: Tenable assesses that espionage appears to be Salt Typhoon's primary objective. Its analysis lists five CVEs known to have been exploited by the group: CVE-2021-26855, CVE-2022-3236, CVE-2023-48788, CVE-2024-21887, and CVE-2023-46805.
location: Tenable article, sections: Objectives and Known CVEs commonly exploited by Salt Typhoon
